question: When a learned low-dimensional activation subspace can interchange a high-level feature and change a language model's output, what additional evidence is required before treating that subspace as a faithful representation actually used by the model rather than an out-of-distribution intervention that activates a dormant pathway?

key_findings.claim: The paper identifies a real non-identifiability in subspace activation patching: end-to-end causal success alone does not establish that the patched direction carries the feature through the model's normal computation.
key_findings.evidence: A direction can mix a feature-correlated component in the kernel of the next output map with a normally inactive but output-causal component. Patching transfers the scalar variation measured along the disconnected component into the causal component, producing the target behavior even though neither component is a normally used mediator. This cleanly separates intervention efficacy from representational and mechanistic faithfulness.

key_findings.claim: The distilled linear example proves the proposed mechanism can occur exactly, but it also makes clear that the label 'illusion' depends on a preferred component basis and architectural decomposition.
key_findings.evidence: In the three-dimensional identity-network example, one hidden direction varies with the input but is output-null, a second is constant on the data but can control the output, and their normalized sum patches perfectly. Appendix A.3 rotates the hidden basis so that the same direction becomes a direct meaningful channel, and the Discussion concedes that arbitrary reparameterizations across component boundaries weaken the illusory/faithful distinction.

anchors.section: Section 8, importance of correct model units

key_findings.claim: On GPT-2 Small IOI, the layer-8 post-GELU MLP direction found by DAS has the signature of the illusion, while full-component patching says the MLP as a whole is not a useful mediator.
key_findings.evidence: The learned one-dimensional v_MLP yields 46.7% mean FLDD but only 4.2% interchange accuracy; its row-space component yields 13.5% and 0.2%, its null-space component 0% and 0%, and patching the full MLP yields -8% and 0%. The null component has norm about 0.65 and the row component about 0.75. Thus scalar variation from a large output-null component is necessary for the mixed intervention even though the full MLP contribution is negligible.

key_findings.claim: The headline 46.7% IOI patch effect should not be read as behavior interchange on roughly half the examples: actual answer flipping is only 4.2%, and the reported mean FLDD can be sensitive to per-example division by a small clean logit difference.
key_findings.evidence: FLDD is defined as the mean of 1 minus patched logit difference divided by clean logit difference. The authors report that more than 99% of examples have a positive clean denominator and the mean is about 3.5, but provide no denominator distribution, clipping, median, bootstrap interval, or sensitivity analysis. Table 1 explicitly separates 46.7% FLDD from 4.2% interchange accuracy. The continuous metric is useful for detecting partial contributions, but it does not by itself show that the model behaves as if the high-level feature changed at the prediction level.

key_findings.claim: The residual-stream success case supplies much stronger convergent evidence, but it is not a ground-truth proof of faithfulness because its 'causally relevant subspace' is only a task-specific proxy.
key_findings.evidence: v_resid gives 140.7% FLDD and 74.8% interchange accuracy, remains strong after the proxy-rowspace restriction, has cosine 0.78 with the downstream gradient, is written by S-inhibition heads, and generalizes qualitatively on OpenWebText. However, the paper explicitly finds no nontrivial subspace in the kernel of all downstream components: it defines causal relevance using only the stacked query matrices of three name-mover heads. All downstream query row spaces span the full residual stream, so the null/row diagnostic cannot rule out other pathways. The authors also acknowledge that no formal ground-truth mechanistic explanation is available.

anchors.section: Section 5.1, proxy causal subspace and footnote 7

key_findings.claim: The held-out IOI split is a genuine strength, yet the paper does not report enough replication detail to quantify optimizer stability or uncertainty.
key_findings.evidence: The test set uses disjoint halves of 216 names, 144 objects, and 75 places and an unseen third template; GPT-2 Small attains about 91% task accuracy. DAS is described as Adam over 'several hundred' patching pairs and results are said to be similar with more examples, but exact train/test intervention counts, learning schedule, random seeds, repeat-to-repeat dispersion, and confidence intervals are absent. Appendix B.7 demonstrates that overfitting occurs with two-name training, reinforcing the need for explicit stability reporting.

key_findings.claim: The random-MLP experiment supports the existence of optimization-induced intervention channels, but it does not actually replace MLP8 and therefore cannot show that a random installed layer normally supports IOI.
key_findings.evidence: To avoid nonsensical generations, the authors keep the real MLP8 in the network, run a random auxiliary MLP, learn a DAS subspace in its activations, and add the auxiliary patched-minus-unpatched output delta to the real MLP8 output. This is an injected residual perturbation, not an ablation or replacement of the trained component. Finding a strong delta direction is consistent with high-dimensional controllability, but it is weaker than the stated intuition that the MLP computation itself does not matter.

key_findings.claim: The illusion persists for a learned 100-dimensional MLP subspace, so it is not merely a one-vector curiosity, although the diagnostic compares different-dimensional interventions.
key_findings.evidence: The 100-dimensional MLP8 subspace reaches 62% FLDD and 13% interchange accuracy, versus 190% and 89% for the residual subspace. Expanding each basis into separate null- and row-space pieces and patching their orthonormalized 200-dimensional span leaves the residual patch strong (200%, 86%) but reduces the MLP patch to 17%, 2%. This supports mixed null/causal coupling, while the original and diagnostic interventions are not dimension-matched and should not be described as a controlled ablation of only one component.

key_findings.claim: The factual-recall experiment exhibits the same qualitative MLP illusion, but its evidentiary scope is narrow: each fact-specific direction is optimized and evaluated on the same seen pair within a set of only 40 pairs over eight GPT-2 XL relations.
key_findings.evidence: The study filters the first 1,000 CounterFact entries to facts GPT-2 XL recalls, forms same-relation pairs, and samples five pairs for each of eight eligible relations. For each pair it uses DAS to optimize the source-to-base object switch and reports that same pair's patch effect; there is no locked held-out source/base combination for the learned direction. The figures show the effect disappearing under full-MLP or rowspace-only patches, but a one-pair optimizer can memorize a control direction rather than recover a reusable representation. The paper also omits neighborhood facts, paraphrases, relation transfer, other models, and restart uncertainty.

key_findings.claim: The ROME reformulation is a useful exact optimization characterization, but its notion of minimal change is only total output variance under an imposed second-moment model, not semantic locality or factual specificity.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma D.1 derives the standard rank-one update as minimizing trace covariance of the extra MLP output subject to mapping one key to one value, with x modeled as zero-mean Gaussian with covariance equal to an empirical uncentered second moment. The algebra is sound given positive-definite Sigma and the constraint, but Gaussianity is unnecessary for the quadratic result and does not validate the distributional model. Minimizing this local second-moment quantity does not guarantee paraphrase generalization, neighborhood preservation, downstream semantic consistency, or low ripple effects.

key_findings.claim: The activation-patch-to-rank-one-edit correspondence is exact only for the patched activation at one token; similarity elsewhere is an empirical observation on the same small factual set, not a model-wide equivalence theorem.
key_findings.evidence: Lemma D.2 constructs a rank-one update whose added MLP output equals one specific subspace patch at token t_A on prompt A. Other tokens and prompts receive b-transformed updates, so the global computations differ. Figures 27-28 report similar target logit differences and edit success across layers for the 40 fact pairs, but omit CounterFact paraphrases, specificity/neighborhood scores, downstream ripple, sequential edits, and independent facts. The paper itself calls the relationship approximate outside the matched token.

key_findings.claim: The reverse ROME-to-'subspace intervention' construction is not, as written, an intervention that sets an orthogonal subspace projection to zero because it never constrains the direction to unit norm.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix D.7 defines x' = x + (c - v^T x)v and derives c = 0, then chooses v = alpha W_out^+ a + u and grid-searches alpha, typically alpha squared = 0.05. The map x -> x - (v^T x)v sets v^T x' to zero only when ||v||=1; otherwise it is a general rank-one linear transformation and is not idempotent. The optimization includes no ||v||=1 constraint. Therefore this direction of the claimed correspondence is between a rank-one weight update and a rank-one activation map, not necessarily a genuine projection-setting subspace intervention.

key_findings.claim: The prevalence argument establishes abundant directions capable of steering an MLP output, not that such directions are represented, used, dormant in the relevant causal sense, or likely to be selected under realistic validation.
key_findings.evidence: If W_out has full row rank, W_out^+v can output any residual direction, while the large kernel supplies disconnected directions. This is an algebraic controllability fact. The correlated-direction step additionally assumes a residual feature is linearly separable, that the pre-GELU map is approximately linear, and that GELU plus kernel projection preserves relevant geometry. Existence of an out-of-distribution steerable direction does not imply the model normally encodes or routes the high-level variable through that direction, and full-rank evidence is shown only for GPT-2 Small.

key_findings.claim: The empirical geometry argument in Appendix E is incomplete and much weaker than the exact property used by its theorem.
key_findings.evidence: Across 1,000 OpenWebText documents, the paper regresses 250,000 inner products per layer and reports R-squared near or above 0.8 except layer 0, but the manuscript still contains literal 'Table TODO' and 'Figure TODO' placeholders. Figure 29 shows heterogeneous clusters and outliers. Quadruples share activations and documents, so they are not 250,000 independent observations. More importantly, an approximate marginal regression fit does not establish a uniform pairwise geometry bound or preserve classification margins, whereas Lemma E.1 assumes exact equality with zero intercept for every distinct quadruple.

anchors.section: Appendix E.3-E.4, Equation 7 and TODO placeholders

key_findings.claim: Lemma E.1 is false as stated for small samples and its proof applies the hypothesis outside its declared domain, so it does not rigorously establish preservation of linear separability.
key_findings.evidence: The lemma assumes inner-product equality only for four distinct indices i,j,k,l. For n less than 4 the condition is vacuous, yet f may map two separable points to the same point, directly contradicting the conclusion. In the proof, support-vector differences (x_sj - x_sj+1) are paired with arbitrary class-opposite (x_i - x_j); these index pairs can overlap, so the four-distinct hypothesis cannot be invoked. Even a corrected exact lemma would not bridge the empirical approximate R-squared result without a quantitative margin/error bound.

key_findings.claim: Appendix A.2 contains a visually confirmed false printed equality in the proof of Lemma A.1; the intended theorem is salvageable by an obvious correction, but the published derivation is not literally valid.
key_findings.evidence: Strong dormancy assumes v_dormant^T act_A = v_dormant^T act_B = c. The proof instead prints that it used v_dormant^T act_A = v_disconnected^T act_B to remove the dormant term. Direct inspection of the rendered PDF confirms this is not an OCR artifact. Replacing the printed right-hand side with v_dormant^T act_B restores the cos(alpha)sin(alpha) derivation.

key_findings.claim: The most durable contribution is a validation doctrine—prefer genuine bottlenecks and triangulate patching with normal-activation evidence, writers/readers, full-component controls, and null/row decompositions—rather than a universal rejection of DAS or linear subspaces.
key_findings.evidence: The authors explicitly show both an illusory MLP direction and a comparatively well-supported residual-stream direction, recommend residual bottlenecks, and call for validation beyond end-to-end success. Their own gauge-dependence and ground-truth discussion, together with the direct 2024 rebuttal, means 'illusion' is best treated as a falsifiable warning about intervention semantics and explanatory parsimony, not proof that a learned causal abstraction is meaningless whenever it has any nullspace component.

method.core_idea: Decompose a learned patching direction relative to the next component's output map, distinguish feature-correlated but output-null variation from normally dormant causal controllability, and require evidence that the same direction participates in ordinary computation rather than only under intervention.
method.mechanism: Formalize one- and higher-dimensional activation patching; construct an exact disconnected-plus-dormant toy example; use DAS to learn IOI position and factual-recall subspaces in GPT-2 Small/XL; project MLP directions into ker(W_out) and its orthogonal complement; compare mixed, component-only, and full-component patches; contrast these with a residual-stream direction informed by the known IOI circuit and downstream gradients; derive local correspondences between rank-one activation maps and ROME edits; and argue that wide full-rank MLPs generically contain output-causal and feature-correlated kernel directions.
assumptions: A high-level variable has a sufficiently well-defined source/base intervention semantics for paired examples.
DAS optimization generalizes beyond its intervention training pairs rather than selecting dataset-specific or optimizer-specific directions.
The selected architectural component boundaries are privileged enough that cross-boundary reparameterizations should count as less parsimonious explanations.
The kernel of an MLP down-projection exactly captures directions disconnected from every downstream effect at that intervention location.
A row-space component with little natural variation but strong steering ability is appropriately described as dormant rather than merely out-of-distribution controllability.
Full-component patching is a meaningful control for whether the component normally mediates the target signal despite possible within-component cancellation.
The IOI circuit analysis correctly identifies S-inhibition and name-mover heads as the principal normal pathway.
The stacked query matrices of three name movers are an adequate task-specific proxy for downstream causal relevance in the residual stream.
Mean FLDD is stable and scientifically meaningful despite its per-example clean-logit denominator.
A held-out split over names, objects, places, and one template adequately samples the intended IOI distribution.
Forty CounterFact pairs across eight relations are sufficient to establish the factual-recall phenomenon across layers.
ROME's empirical uncentered second moment is positive definite or suitably regularized for inverse-based formulas.
Local matching of an MLP output at one token predicts comparable downstream model behavior under a rank-one weight edit.
A rank-one activation map without an explicit unit-norm constraint can be interpreted as setting a subspace projection.
GPT-2 Small MLP input/output matrices being numerically full rank is representative of transformer MLPs more generally.
Layer normalization followed by a linear map is sufficiently close to linear on the data distribution for residual separability to transfer pre-GELU.
Approximate inner-product regression after GELU and kernel projection is strong enough to preserve task-relevant separation margins.
OpenWebText activation samples and random residual directions are representative of naturally occurring high-level features.

techniques.role: Replaces only the orthogonal projection of a base activation on a learned subspace with the corresponding source projection.
Optimizes orthogonal activation directions or subspaces whose interchange interventions match a high-level variable.
Separates feature-correlated output-null variation from components that can affect the next residual update.
Tests whether transferring the entire MLP or residual activation produces the same causal effect as a selected subspace.
Computes the residual direction that most increases name-mover attention to one name over the other.
Checks which upstream heads write a candidate residual direction and which downstream query maps read it.
Evaluates DAS on unseen names, objects, places, and a withheld prompt template.
Demonstrates that an auxiliary random nonlinear map can furnish a strong injected residual perturbation direction.
Expresses ROME as a constrained minimum-output-variance rank-one update under an empirical second moment.
Constructs a weight update matching a one-dimensional activation patch at a selected prompt token.
Checks numerical full rank of GPT-2 Small MLP input and output matrices.
Regresses post-GELU kernel-projected difference inner products on pre-GELU difference inner products over OpenWebText.
Tests linear regression/classification recovery of synthetic residual directions from post-GELU MLP activations.

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small IOI, layer-8 post-GELU MLP direction learned by DAS and evaluated on held-out lexical items and template
evaluations.metric: Mean fractional logit-difference decrease (FLDD) and interchange accuracy
evaluations.result: v_MLP: 46.7% FLDD, 4.2% interchange; row component: 13.5%, 0.2%; null component: 0%, 0%; full MLP: -8%, 0%. The mixed direction has null/row norms about 0.65/0.75.
evaluations.baseline: Full-component patch, isolated kernel and row-space components, and prior IOI circuit attribution

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small IOI, layer-8 residual-stream candidate and downstream-gradient candidate
evaluations.metric: FLDD, interchange accuracy, cosine similarity, proxy-rowspace norm, feature separation, and upstream writer analysis
evaluations.result: v_resid: 140.7%/74.8%; proxy-row component: 127.5%/63.1%; full residual: 123.6%/54.8%. v_resid and v_grad have cosine about 0.78 and 91%/98% of their norms in the three-name-mover query proxy rowspace; S-inhibition heads selectively write v_resid.
evaluations.baseline: Random-vector cosine scale near 1/sqrt(768), proxy-null components, full residual patch, and manually identified IOI circuit

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small IOI, 100-dimensional MLP and residual subspaces
evaluations.metric: FLDD and interchange accuracy before and after null/row basis expansion
evaluations.result: Original residual/MLP subspaces reach 190%/89% and 62%/13%. Patching the orthonormalized 200-dimensional spans of separately projected basis vectors gives 200%/86% for residual and 17%/2% for MLP.

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small IOI with an auxiliary randomly initialized MLP matched in output norm
evaluations.metric: DAS-optimized effect on IOI logit difference
evaluations.result: The injected patched-minus-unpatched delta from the random auxiliary MLP produces a direction reported stronger than v_MLP.
evaluations.baseline: The learned layer-8 MLP direction; the actual trained MLP remains installed

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 XL factual recall on 40 CounterFact pairs from eight relations
evaluations.metric: Target-versus-original object logit difference and edit success across intervention layers
evaluations.result: DAS one-dimensional MLP patches frequently change the recalled object; the effect largely disappears for the row component or full MLP patch.
evaluations.baseline: Full hidden-MLP transfer and causally relevant rowspace-only patch

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 XL ROME and rank-one activation-map correspondence on the same factual pairs
evaluations.metric: Rewrite success, layerwise target logit difference, direction cosine, and output variance
evaluations.result: Constructed rank-one edits closely track one-dimensional patches in target logits and success; zero-setting activation maps can approximate ROME's rewrite and variance behavior across middle layers for grid-chosen alpha.
evaluations.baseline: ROME update and DAS activation patch; no paraphrase, neighborhood, sequential-edit, or ripple baseline

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small OpenWebText inner-product geometry through GELU and projection onto ker(W_out)
evaluations.metric: Per-layer linear-regression R-squared over 250,000 sampled quadruple measurements
evaluations.result: R-squared is roughly 0.8 or higher in most layers except layer 0; rendered plots show layer-dependent clusters and outliers. The text retains unresolved Table/Figure TODO references.
evaluations.baseline: Identity-like linear geometry preservation before the nonlinear and kernel-projection map

evaluations.setting: Recovery of random residual directions from post-GELU GPT-2 Small MLP activations
evaluations.metric: Held-out regression R-squared/MSE and binary classification accuracy under injected direction scales
evaluations.result: Regression reports R-squared 0.71 +/- 0.17, MSE 0.31 +/- 0.18, p < 0.005; mean binary accuracy is 0.69, 0.83, 0.87, and 0.996 for z = 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, and 0.1.

limitations: The empirical study covers only GPT-2 Small on IOI and GPT-2 XL on a tiny factual-pair subset; no model-family, scale, architecture, or training-run replication is reported.
The authors explicitly lack a formal ground-truth definition of mechanistic explanation, so classifying a direction as illusory relies on architectural boundaries and parsimony judgments.
The toy illusion is basis dependent and becomes a direct meaningful channel under a hidden-space rotation.
The IOI DAS training set is described only as several hundred pairs, and exact evaluation counts, seeds, optimizer schedules, and run-to-run variance are missing.
Mean FLDD divides by each example's clean logit difference and is reported without denominator sensitivity, robust summaries, or uncertainty intervals.
The principal MLP result flips the answer in only 4.2% of patches despite a 46.7% mean FLDD.
The residual-stream causal relevance diagnostic uses three name-mover query matrices because the true joint downstream rowspace is the entire residual space.
OpenWebText examples for the residual direction are qualitative extrema rather than a preregistered quantitative out-of-distribution benchmark.
The random-MLP test injects an auxiliary delta into the intact trained network instead of replacing or ablating MLP8.
The high-dimensional null/row diagnostic compares a 100-dimensional learned subspace with a potentially 200-dimensional expanded span.
The factual study uses only 40 pairs from eight relations, and each fact-specific DAS direction is trained and evaluated on its same single pair rather than locked held-out source/base combinations.
The factual correspondence omits standard edit locality, paraphrase, neighborhood, ripple, sequential-edit, and consistency metrics.
Lemma D.2 guarantees equality only at one token on one prompt, not equivalence of the full intervened networks.
The ROME-to-activation construction lacks the unit-norm constraint required for its map to set an orthogonal subspace projection to zero.
The ROME variance objective is based on a local empirical second moment and does not certify semantic minimality.
The prevalence argument proves directional controllability under full row rank, not natural representation or normal causal use.
Full-rank and geometry evidence is limited to GPT-2 Small and sampled activations.
The geometry regression uses highly dependent measurements and point-fit R-squared rather than a uniform distortion or classification-margin guarantee.
The claim that patches go off-manifold is not quantified with activation density, nearest-neighbor or Mahalanobis distance, GELU saturation, local Jacobians, or OOD-matched controls.

Nullspace overlap is not sufficient for unfaithfulness: on an oblique data manifold, a genuinely predictive causal direction can contain an immediate-output-null component, and rowspace projection can destroy its discriminating coefficient.
Appendix E.3 contains unresolved 'Table TODO' and 'Figure TODO' placeholders.
Lemma E.1 is false as stated for n < 4 and its proof violates its own all-distinct-index premise.
Lemma A.1's displayed proof contains a confirmed incorrect equality, although the intended argument is easily repaired.
No independent reproduction or blinded comparison of competing interpretability hypotheses is included.
failure_modes: DAS selects a mixed null/causal direction that changes outputs while bypassing the feature's normal route.
A large controllable but off-manifold direction is mislabeled as a naturally represented semantic feature.
A favorable mean FLDD is driven by examples with small clean-logit denominators while behavior rarely flips.
A full-component patch masks real countervailing subcircuits, causing a genuinely used representation to be rejected as illusory.
Conversely, within-component cancellation is invoked post hoc to rescue an arbitrary intervention direction from a failed full-component control.
The selected clean/corrupt prompt pairing changes multiple latent variables despite matching the named high-level feature.
A learned subspace overfits lexical items, templates, relations, or a small number of source/base pairs.
A proxy downstream reader set omits alternate or backup pathways and gives a false impression that disconnected components were removed.
A random auxiliary network supplies an adversarial perturbation channel that is mistaken for evidence about an installed model component.
A rank-one edit matches one patched token but changes unrelated tokens, prompts, or facts through its global weight update.
A non-unit vector in x - vv^T x is called a projection intervention even though it neither zeros the coordinate nor acts idempotently.
Empirical covariance inversion is ill-conditioned and turns a minimum-variance edit into a high-amplitude unstable direction.
Approximate average geometry preservation hides low-margin examples for which GELU and projection destroy separability.
Dependent quadruple measurements inflate apparent statistical evidence for geometry preservation.
Component-level explanations change under equivalent reparameterizations, so conclusions reflect the chosen gauge more than model function.
An intervention benchmark rewards output control without separately measuring natural activation, necessity, sufficiency, compositionality, and distributional validity.
reusable_insights: Treat intervention success, information encoding, normal causal use, and human interpretability as four separate claims requiring separate tests.
For a candidate direction inside a linear-output component, decompose it into the output map's kernel and row space before interpreting it.
Always compare a low-dimensional patch with full-component transfer and with patches of the decomposed components.
Prefer intervention locations that are genuine communication bottlenecks, such as the residual stream, when the scientific question permits it.
Triangulate a feature by identifying ordinary upstream writers, downstream readers, natural activation distributions, and task-preserving ablations.
Report both continuous causal-effect metrics and actual behavior interchange, with denominator diagnostics and uncertainty.
Use factor-disjoint held-out splits and multiple optimizer seeds for learned intervention subspaces.
A full-row-rank map guarantees controllability, not representation; steering directions need an in-distribution natural-use test.
State the exact estimand and intervention distribution so causal fidelity claims can receive confidence intervals or anytime-valid certification.
When claiming an equivalence between activation and weight interventions, specify whether it holds at one token, one prompt, in expectation, or model-wide.
Validate model edits on paraphrases, neighborhoods, logical consequences, ripple effects, and long edit sequences rather than rewrite success alone.
Make projection operators explicit: either normalize v or use v(v^T v)^{-1}v^T.
Use semi-synthetic models with known circuits to evaluate whether a method recovers normal mechanisms rather than merely effective controls.
Replace average R-squared geometry arguments with quantitative distortion bounds relative to the classifier margin.
Audit theorem statements for degenerate sample sizes and index-overlap cases before using them to justify an empirical prevalence claim.
Declare the architectural decomposition or gauge under which an explanation is meant to be sparse and human-meaningful.
open_questions: Can a benchmark jointly score intervention efficacy, in-distribution support, normal causal use, explanation sparsity, and invariance under benign reparameterization?
What is the weakest set of writer/reader and necessity/sufficiency tests that rules out dormant-pathway illusions with a formal guarantee?
Can DAS be regularized toward naturally occupied activation manifolds or minimal Mahalanobis-distance interventions without suppressing genuinely distributed features?
How stable are learned subspaces across seeds, data resampling, model checkpoints, scales, and equivalent prompt families?
Which component boundaries are functionally privileged, and can that privilege be derived from conditional independence, modularity, sparsity, or training dynamics rather than intuition?
Can gauge-invariant equivalence classes of mechanistic explanations preserve human-readable structure?
How often do low-dimensional directions that control outputs also mediate the same variable under purely observational natural activations?
Does the null-plus-dormant mechanism remain prevalent in gated MLPs, mixture-of-experts models, recurrent architectures, and modern instruction-tuned LLMs?
Can InterpBench-style known-circuit transformers be augmented with deliberately planted dormant pathways to measure false-discovery rates?
What robust alternative to per-example fractional logit change best measures partial circuit contributions without denominator pathologies?
Can rank-one edit/patch correspondences predict paraphrase generalization, specificity, downstream consequences, and edit interference at scale?
Under what norm and activation distribution should edit minimality be defined so that it tracks semantic locality?
What unit-normalized solution, if any, gives a principled ROME-to-orthogonal-subspace projection correspondence?
Can approximate geometry preservation through MLP nonlinearities be proved with explicit error and classification-margin dependence?
How much of the 2024 direct rebuttal is resolved by preregistered held-out intervention distributions and component-level controls?
Can certified interventional fidelity be combined with mechanistic falsification tests so statistically stable effects are not mistaken for faithful explanations?

competitive_landscape.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct method predecessor: Distributed Alignment Search
competitive_landscape.difference: Geiger et al. introduce DAS and evaluate alignment through distributed interchange intervention accuracy under a causal-abstraction framework. The reviewed paper does not replace DAS; it shows that an optimized alignment with the desired end-to-end counterfactual can exploit output-null variation and a dormant causal channel unless the representation's ordinary mechanistic role is separately validated.

competitive_landscape.title: A Reply to Makelov et al. (2023)'s 'Interpretability Illusion' Arguments
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. argue that Makelov et al.'s nullspace-based illusion definition can reject intuitive desirable representations and that the reported pathologies depend on training and evaluation choices. Their independent IOI experiments agree that the MLP activation has about 4% IIA while the layer-8 residual direction reaches about 70%, and trace the signal through attention heads. This makes the reviewed paper's empirical warning strong but its normative label contested.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
competitive_landscape.relationship: manual-circuit ground for the IOI case study
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. identify S-inhibition, name-mover, backup, duplicate-token, and negative heads using multiple interventions and quantify faithfulness, completeness, and minimality. The reviewed paper leverages that component-level circuit as a prior to distinguish a plausible residual feature from an MLP subspace, but the manual circuit is itself incomplete and does not constitute formal ground truth.

competitive_landscape.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
competitive_landscape.difference: Meng et al. combine causal tracing with the ROME rank-one editor and evaluate rewrite, paraphrase, and neighborhood behavior on CounterFact. The reviewed paper gives a useful variance-minimization reformulation and dormant-pathway account, but its 40-pair correspondence tests only rewrite-oriented outputs and therefore do not reproduce ROME's broader locality/generalization evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Localization Inform Editing? Surprising Differences in Causality-Based Localization vs. Knowledge Editing in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct empirical motivation and competing explanation
competitive_landscape.difference: Hase et al. show on hundreds of facts and multiple robustness variants that causal-tracing localization adds little predictive value for the best editing layer beyond layer identity. The reviewed paper proposes dormant pathways and rank-one controllability as a mechanistic explanation, but tests a much smaller fact set and does not establish that its mechanism quantitatively explains Hase et al.'s full localization-editing mismatch.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang and Nanda systematically vary patching metrics and corruption/patch choices, demonstrating that localization conclusions depend strongly on experimental design. The reviewed paper contributes a distinct algebraic failure mode inside learned subspaces; together they imply that both the intervention operator and its measurement protocol must be audited.

competitive_landscape.title: How to use and interpret activation patching
competitive_landscape.difference: Heimersheim and Nanda synthesize what activation patching can support, metric pitfalls, corruption choices, and circuit-level interpretation. It operationalizes the reviewed paper's caution for practitioners but is guidance rather than a benchmark with known mechanisms or a formal dormant-pathway detector.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics Are Not Robust
competitive_landscape.difference: Miller, Chughtai, and Saunders show that circuit faithfulness scores vary substantially under reasonable ablation implementations, including on IOI. Their result generalizes the reviewed paper's central lesson from subspace mixing to circuit evaluation: measured faithfulness is partly a property of the intervention distribution and replacement rule.

competitive_landscape.title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
competitive_landscape.difference: InterpBench creates realistic semi-synthetic transformers whose intended circuits are known and whose non-circuit nodes are prevented from affecting outputs. It directly addresses the reviewed paper's acknowledged ground-truth problem and could measure whether subspace methods recover normal mechanisms rather than only successful interventions, although planted models may not capture all natural-model degeneracies.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks proceedings version

competitive_landscape.title: Identifying Functionally Important Features with End-to-End Sparse Dictionary Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Braun et al. train sparse dictionaries to preserve the model's output distribution when inserted end to end, explicitly targeting functional importance rather than activation reconstruction. This reduces one proxy gap but does not by itself rule out dormant or off-manifold intervention features; the reviewed paper suggests adding normal-use and reader/writer diagnostics to such objectives.

competitive_landscape.title: Combining Causal Models for More Accurate Abstractions of Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Pislar et al. combine multiple simple high-level causal models and expose a trade-off between coverage and interchange-intervention faithfulness. This addresses hypothesis misspecification and input-dependent algorithms, while the reviewed paper highlights a different identifiability issue: even high intervention agreement can be achieved by a low-level alignment that is mechanistically perverse under the chosen decomposition.

competitive_landscape.title: The Non-Linear Representation Dilemma: Is Causal Abstraction Enough for Mechanistic Interpretability?
competitive_landscape.difference: Sutter et al. prove that sufficiently expressive alignment maps can map essentially any network to any algorithm, making unconstrained causal abstraction trivial. Their impossibility result complements the reviewed paper's constructive linear counterexample and sharpens why alignment classes need simplicity, geometry, and normal-use constraints.

competitive_landscape.title: Certified Interventional Fidelity: Anytime-Valid, Adaptive Evaluation of Causal Claims in Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Asiaee defines bounded interventional fidelity estimands over explicit input and intervention distributions and supplies confidence sequences robust to adaptive sampling, with IOI experiments. It directly fixes the reviewed paper's missing uncertainty and intervention-distribution specification, but statistical certification of a patching effect cannot alone certify that the chosen subspace is the model's normal mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Interpretability at Scale: Identifying Causal Mechanisms in Alpaca
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. replace DAS's remaining discrete search with learned boundaries and report robust high-level boolean alignments in Alpaca-7B across inputs and instructions. It extends the method to a much larger model, but the reviewed paper implies that held-out interchange accuracy still needs ordinary-pathway and nullspace diagnostics before being interpreted as a unique internal mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Conmy et al.'s ACDC greedily prunes model edges under activation patching and validates recovery of known circuit component types. It searches architectural graph structure rather than arbitrary activation bases, which supplies a stronger parsimony prior, but it remains sensitive to the metric, corruption, replacement distribution, and incompleteness of reference circuits.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Differentiating Concepts: Interpreting LM Behavior via Causal Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Goyal et al. learn sparse behavior-changing latent concepts without predefined labels and test ground-truth recovery in synthetic and semi-synthetic settings plus LM refusal. Their constrained representation-learning objective attacks label and supervision limitations, while the reviewed paper warns that any behavior-changing direction still needs natural-use and off-manifold checks.

competitive_landscape.title: pyvene: A Library for Understanding and Improving PyTorch Models via Interventions
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu et al. provide a unified implementation layer for static and trainable interventions, causal abstraction, and localization across PyTorch modules. This improves reproducibility and makes intervention semantics explicit in code, but software unification does not resolve which counterfactual replacements are scientifically identifying.

competitive_landscape.title: CausalGym: Benchmarking causal interpretability methods on linguistic tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: CausalGym evaluates DAS-style distributed interventions alongside simple representation baselines on controlled linguistic variables and includes selectivity and arbitrary-mapping controls. It provides the matched random/simple-direction protocol absent from the reviewed IOI and one-pair factual studies, though controlled linguistic tasks do not resolve natural-mechanism ground truth in open-ended behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: Everything, Everywhere, All at Once: Is Mechanistic Interpretability Identifiable?
competitive_landscape.difference: Meloux et al. enumerate circuits, algorithms, and alignment subspaces in small networks and find multiple incompatible explanations satisfying standard criteria for both where-then-what and what-then-where strategies. This generalizes the reviewed paper's basis-dependent counterexample: even without a null-plus-dormant splice, output faithfulness need not identify a unique explanation.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Cunningham et al. learn an overcomplete sparse dictionary and identify finer-grained causally relevant IOI features, rather than directly optimizing a source-to-base control direction. Sparsity and reconstruction offer a different natural-activation prior, but SAE features can still split, combine, or control behavior without a stable context-general downstream function.

competitive_landscape.title: An Interpretability Illusion for BERT
competitive_landscape.difference: Bolukbasi et al. show that apparently simple neuron or direction concepts can arise from BERT embedding geometry and narrow corpus slices, motivating tests across datasets. The reviewed paper's narrower novelty is causal: its patched direction splices an output-null correlate with a dormant output-effective direction, so it can control behavior despite mislocalizing normal mediation.

competitive_landscape.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Karvonen et al. evaluate more than 200 sparse autoencoders across interpretability, disentanglement, and practical control metrics and find proxy gains do not reliably predict practical utility. This reinforces the reviewed paper's proxy warning and supplies breadth it lacks, while focusing on SAE dictionaries rather than direct dormant-pathway detection.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Encode Both Concepts and Functions: The Downstream Geometry of Feature Effects
competitive_landscape.difference: Hoang et al.'s FEGA removes the same active SAE feature across contexts and studies the cloud of resulting logit changes, finding stable one-dimensional effects rare and distinguishing value-like from context-dependent pointer-like features. It operationalizes the reviewed paper's control-versus-reusable-function distinction beyond a single source/base pair.

competitive_landscape.title: Causal Abstraction: A Theoretical Foundation for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Geiger et al. formalize causal abstraction for arbitrary mechanism transformations and unify patching, tracing, scrubbing, concept erasure, DAS, sparse autoencoders, and steering. The reviewed paper supplies a concrete warning that graded interventional faithfulness is not by itself a human-readable or decomposition-invariant identification criterion.
competitive_landscape.source_version: Journal of Machine Learning Research 26(184), 2025 version of record

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims that naive low-dimensional activation patching can hallucinate meaningful subspaces by using feature-correlated causally disconnected components to activate dormant output-causal pathways; it demonstrates the phenomenon in an exact toy model, GPT-2 IOI, and factual recall, links it to rank-one model editing, argues it should be prevalent, and proposes additional validations for faithful subspaces.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The exact construction and MLP null/row experiments convincingly show that end-to-end patch success is insufficient. The IOI comparison supplies unusually rich positive and negative controls, and the local activation-patch-to-rank-one-edit construction is mathematically useful. The factual sample is small, the reverse edit-to-subspace construction omits unit normalization, the prevalence theorem has a false-as-stated lemma and incomplete empirical bridge, and the paper concedes basis dependence and absence of formal ground truth.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The core dormant-pathway counterexample is a novel and lasting falsification tool, not a universal impossibility result for DAS. Its strongest contribution is to force causal representation work to state the intervention distribution and distinguish controllability from normal use. Claims of practical prevalence and approximate equivalence are substantially less established than the central counterexample. The direct 2024 rebuttal correctly narrows the normative conclusion: a nullspace component is evidence to investigate, not an automatic disqualifier, because explanation quality also depends on the chosen causal model, training distribution, and privileged decomposition. Subsequent work on known-circuit benchmarks, robust faithfulness metrics, constrained causal concepts, and certified interventional estimands provides concrete routes to make the warning testable.

reviewer_notes: Read all 58 cached pages, including the full main text, proofs in Appendices A and D-E, IOI and factual-recall experimental details, all tables, and direct rendered-PDF inspections of the printed Lemma A.1 equality and Appendix E figures. The cached text required OCR on pages 52-53, so figure-heavy pages 45-46 and 57-58 were inspected visually. Current competing primary sources were checked through arXiv, OpenReview, ACL Anthology, official NeurIPS proceedings, and PMLR through 2026-08-23. Two distinctions govern this review: an output-effective direction is not necessarily a naturally used representation, and a stable interventional estimand is not necessarily a privileged mechanistic explanation. The 2024 direct reply is included because it materially contests the paper's criterion and reproduces the main IOI localization contrast.
